steelScrap.label: Steel scrap (end-of-life, closed-loop recycling)
steelScrap.unit: kg CO2e potential net benefit per kg steel scrap
steelScrap.sourceUnit: kg CO2-e saved per kg end-of-life steel scrap recycled
steelScrap.source: Broadbent, Clare. “Steel’s recyclability: demonstrating the benefits of recycling steel to achieve a circular economy.” The International Journal of Life Cycle Assessment, 21(11), 1658–1665.
steelScrap.sourceLocation: Abstract, Results and discussion; reported as a per-kg result, not a numbered table.
steelScrap.boundary: The abstract describes an ISO 14040/44:2006 closed-material-loop recycling methodology, including the burden of using scrap and the benefit of avoided primary steel production. The full article was not accessible for verification of detailed process stages.
steelScrap.assumptions: For all generic steel listings, assumes the listed mass is end-of-life steel scrap recycled into new steel in a closed loop; this is not confirmed per listing.
steelScrap.limitations: Indicative literature benchmark. Geography, scrap grade/yield, transport and detailed system-boundary stages could not be verified from the accessible abstract. Applying it to all steel listings may overstate benefit when the material is not end-of-life scrap or is not recycled closed-loop.

glass.label: Glass (containers and packaging)
glass.unit: kg CO2e potential net benefit per kg material
glass.source: US EPA, Waste Reduction Model (WARM), Version 16
glass.sourceLocation: Materials document, Exhibit 1-4, “Glass” row; model workbook “Summary Data”!C5.
glass.boundary: Net emissions for the post-consumer recycling pathway, referenced at waste generation. The model includes collection and transport to recycling, sorting and processing, recycled-material manufacture, and offsets for avoided virgin-material acquisition and manufacture. The documented boundary includes relevant material and product transportation; it excludes transport from retail/distribution to the consumer.
glass.assumptions: WARM assumes glass waste is containers and packaging and models closed-loop recycling of bottles and jars into the same material.
glass.limitations: Not applicable to flat/plate glass, windows, mirrors, or glass in durable goods.

plastic.label: Mixed plastics (HDPE 40%, PET 60%)
plastic.unit: kg CO2e potential net benefit per kg material
plastic.source: US EPA, Waste Reduction Model (WARM), Version 16
plastic.sourceLocation: Materials document, Exhibit 5-3, “Mixed Plastics” row; model workbook “Summary Data”!C35.
plastic.boundary: Net emissions for the post-consumer recycling pathway, referenced at waste generation. The model includes collection and transport to recycling, sorting and processing, recycled-material manufacture, and offsets for avoided virgin-material acquisition and manufacture. The documented boundary includes relevant material and product transportation; it excludes transport from retail/distribution to the consumer.
plastic.assumptions: WARM defines mixed plastics as 40% HDPE and 60% PET by weight.
plastic.limitations: Category-average estimate only; do not apply to a known resin type or an arbitrary finished plastic product.

paper.label: Mixed paper (general)
paper.unit: kg CO2e potential net benefit per kg material
paper.source: US EPA, Waste Reduction Model (WARM), Version 16
paper.sourceLocation: Materials document, Exhibit 3-7, “Mixed Paper (general)” row; model workbook “Summary Data”!C31.
paper.boundary: Net emissions for the post-consumer recycling pathway, referenced at waste generation. The model includes collection and transport to recycling, sorting and processing, recycled-material manufacture, and offsets for avoided virgin-material acquisition and manufacture. The documented boundary includes relevant material and product transportation; it excludes transport from retail/distribution to the consumer.
paper.assumptions: WARM defines general mixed paper as 48% corrugated containers, 8% magazines/third-class mail, 24% newspaper, and 20% office paper by weight.
paper.limitations: Does not represent board/card specifically or the primarily residential/office mixed-paper categories.
